info.title: QbAutopost API
info.description:
Turns a job folder or a batch of JSON rows into posted QuickBooks Desktop transactions.

This document is **hand-authored** (`src/QbAutopost.Api/wwwroot/openapi.json`): .NET 8 has no built-in OpenAPI generator and Swashbuckle is excluded, so nothing generates it from the code. It is kept honest by `OpenApiDriftTests`, which walks the application's own route table and fails the build when a route is undocumented, an operation has no route, or an operation is missing its summary, its response schema or the scope it needs. `x-required-scope` on each operation is the scope the middleware actually enforces, not a description of it.

The reference page and this document are served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true, and both need the `health:read` scope.

get.summary: Liveness and build facts; never calls QuickBooks or Hermes.
get.description: Answers from in-process state only, so a monitor may poll it every few seconds and still get an answer while a post holds the QuickBooks gateway.

503.description: The host is shutting down.

get.summary: Readiness: settings, prompts, rules, lists, log folder and the job worker.
get.description: `ok` is false only when a check of severity `error` failed; a `warning` keeps `ok` true.

503.description: At least one error-severity check failed.

get.summary: QuickBooks SDK registration, versions and bitness; no company file is opened.
get.description: Answers while QuickBooks is closed, while another company is open, or while a certificate dialog is pending — this is the check that explains a failure that never reached QuickBooks.

200.description: The request processor is registered and the bitness matches.

503.description: The SDK is not usable; `message` says why.

get.summary: One round trip to QuickBooks: is the expected company file open?
get.description: Opens an SDK session, so it waits behind a post in progress for at most `QuickBooks:BusyTimeoutSeconds`.

503.description: QuickBooks is unreachable or busy.

get.summary: Hermes reachability, model name and round-trip latency.
get.description: With `Hermes:Enabled` false the app runs with no model at all and this reports the disabled client.

503.description: Hermes is unreachable.

get.summary: Saved-requests database: reachability, schema state and check latency.
get.description: Looks at the database now. Never includes the connection string. With `Database:ConnectionString` empty the feature is off and this answers 503 with reason `not-configured`; the rest of the API is unaffected. Either `requests:read` (any dashboard user, for the status light) or `health:read` satisfies it.

200.description: The database answered and its schema is current.

503.description: Not configured, unreachable, or the schema is out of date; `reason` says which.

post.summary: A full session round trip, timed step by step.
post.description: Its own budget (`QuickBooks:ConnectionTestTimeoutSeconds`, default 180 s), deliberately longer than the busy timeout: on the owner's server a certificate dialog held the first session 101 s, and a slow answer is not a broken one. Changes nothing.

200.description: The round trip finished; `ok` and `steps` say how it went.

post.summary: Is this company file the configured one, open in QuickBooks, and backed up?
post.description: Read-only: no qbXML is sent. A *different* company file open in QuickBooks is an error, not a warning — it is the one misconfiguration that posts real money into the wrong ledger.

422.description: A check of severity `error` failed; the body lists every check.

post.summary: Would these rows post? The same reader, mapper and gates, stopping short of the SDK call.
post.description: Offline and never writes, so a batch can be checked while the QuickBooks server is shut down. 400 when the request contradicts itself (a control total that does not add up, no rows, too many); 422 when it was understood and a gate held a row.

parameters.name: includeQbXml
parameters.description: Return the qbXML request body as well. It carries every amount and name in the batch, so it is served only to a key holding `qb:debug`; a caller without it is told so rather than left wondering.

422.description: The request was understood and at least one row was held or skipped.

post.summary: Validate the whole payload and, if nothing is held, post all of it — one request, one response.
post.description: Synchronous: no `dryRun`, no `202`, no batch to poll. **All or nothing** — if any row would be held the answer is 422 listing every finding and not one byte reaches QuickBooks; otherwise every row posts and the `txnId`s come back in the same response. The QuickBooks session is taken only if it is free: when a folder job or another post holds it the answer is 409 with `Retry-After`, and nothing is enqueued. The caller holds the connection for the whole post, which for a large batch is minutes, so set a client timeout longer than the largest batch you send — and send an `Idempotency-Key`, because after a lost response it is the only way to get the original `txnId`s back rather than a second posting. `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/transactions` (FR-A-8) is unchanged and still offers `dryRun`, `202` and per-row holds.

200.description: Every row posted. `postId` names the ledger row for `POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/undo`; it is not a resource to poll.

400.description: The request could not be read: a control total that does not add up, too many rows, a malformed row, or `dryRun`/`allowModelAccounts` — neither exists on this route, and sending either is refused rather than ignored.

409.description: QuickBooks is busy with a folder job or another post. Nothing was sent and nothing was queued, so retrying is safe; `Retry-After` says when.

422.description: At least one row would be held, so none was posted. `validation` lists every finding, not the first.

503.description: The backup is too old (FR-11), QuickBooks is unreachable, or the rules file is missing. Nothing was posted in any of these cases.

post.summary: Post JSON rows to QuickBooks and return the batch result.
post.description: The only route that sends transactions to QuickBooks. The batch is on disk before it is queued, so there is always something to poll. `dryRun` (default `DryRunDefault`) ends in `ready` with nothing sent. If the work outlasts `Api:SyncPostTimeoutSeconds` the answer is 202 with a batch to poll and the work carries on; `Prefer: respond-async` asks for that immediately.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: `respond-async` to be answered 202 without waiting.

200.description: The batch finished (or was a dry run).

get.summary: The cached QuickBooks account, vendor and customer names.
get.description: Read from `qb-lists.json`, so it answers while QuickBooks is shut down and never queues behind a post. A `syncedUtc` of `null` with empty lists means the sync has not run yet; it is not an error. Needs `lists:read`, which every dashboard role holds; an API key holding `qb:read` satisfies it too.

200.description: The names as the last sync left them.

post.summary: Read the QuickBooks account, vendor and customer lists into qb-lists.json.
post.description: One read-only message set (active records only). It runs on the single job worker, so it cannot overlap a job or a post. This is the v1 spelling; `POST /api/v1/qb/sync-lists` is the same handler under the pre-M9 name and will go when the legacy routes do (Q-53, Q-69).

200.description: The lists were read and written.

post.summary: Deprecated spelling of POST /api/v1/quickbooks/lists/sync; same handler, same body.
post.description: Kept because callers written before M9 use it. Move to `/api/v1/quickbooks/lists/sync`; this path goes when `Api:LegacyRoutes` is turned off (Q-53).

200.description: The lists were read and written.

get.summary: The batch as last recorded — the poll target for a post that outlasted its budget.
get.description: Read from `result.json`, falling back to `status.json` while the batch is still running, so the answer survives a restart of this process.

post.summary: Delete the transactions this batch posted, one message set on the job worker.
post.description: Each ledger entry is marked `undone` as QuickBooks confirms its delete, so a partial undo is recorded as exactly what happened.

200.description: What was deleted, and what would not delete.

get.summary: Every known job, newest first, optionally filtered by status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Case-insensitive job status.

post.summary: Queue a job folder for analysis (and posting, when it is not a dry run).
post.description: The job id is derived from the folder, so re-submitting the same folder is the same job; `force` re-runs one that already finished.

202.description: The job was accepted and queued.

post.summary: Would this folder run? F1, the statement parse and the G1 reconcile gate, with no job queued.
post.description: Nothing is written into the folder (not even `output/`), no job id is taken and QuickBooks is never called. It stops short of the requirement, the mapper and the duplicate check, so a folder that passes here may still hold lines when it runs.

422.description: The folder would not run; the body is the same shape as the 200.

get.summary: One job: its status, its statements, and what was held, skipped or posted.

post.summary: Post a job that analysed cleanly and is waiting in `ready`.

202.description: The job was queued for posting.

post.summary: Teach the mapper that a description fragment means a named vendor or customer.
post.description: Written atomically into `rules.json` and picked up by the next job or re-post.

200.description: The rule as written, with what it replaced.

post.summary: Teach the mapper which expense account a vendor posts to.
post.description: The account must exist in `qb-lists.json` when the lists have been synced, so a typo is refused here rather than by QuickBooks mid-batch.

200.description: The rule as written, with what it replaced.

get.summary: This document.
get.description: Served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true; otherwise the route is not mapped at all and the answer is 404.

get.summary: The Scalar page that renders this document.
get.description: Served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true. Its script comes from the package, not a CDN, and the "send request" buttons are hidden unless `Api:Reference:AllowTryIt` is true.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password.
post.description: Answers an access token (JWT, HS256, `Auth:Jwt:AccessTokenMinutes`) and sets the refresh cookie `qbautopost_refresh` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/auth`, `Auth:Jwt:RefreshTokenDays`). An unknown email, a wrong password and a disabled account all answer the same `401 invalid-credentials`. `Auth:Lockout:MaxFailedAttempts` wrong passwords lock the account for `Auth:Lockout:LockoutMinutes` (`423 locked-out`). Failed sign-ins are also braked per address and per email by `Api:RateLimits:FailedAuthPerMinute` (`429`). Every failure is recorded in `user_audit`. `503 auth-not-configured` when `Auth:Jwt:SigningKey` is missing; `503 database-unavailable` when the database is not ready.

200.description: Signed in. The refresh cookie is set.

401.description: Wrong credentials: unknown email, wrong password or disabled account. One answer for all three (`invalid-credentials`).

423.description: `locked-out`: too many wrong passwords; `Retry-After` says for how long.

post.summary: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new refresh cookie.
post.description: Takes no body and no header credential: only the `qbautopost_refresh` cookie. The presented token is revoked and its successor set. Presenting a token that was already revoked revokes its whole family (a theft signal) and answers `401`; so does a missing, unknown or expired token, and the cookie is then cleared.

200.description: A new access token; the refresh cookie is replaced.

401.description: `invalid-refresh-token`: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. The cookie is cleared.

post.summary: Sign out: revoke the current refresh token and clear the cookie.
post.description: Revokes the refresh token in the `qbautopost_refresh` cookie (that token only, none of the caller's others), and always clears the cookie. Allowed while a password change is pending.

get.summary: The signed-in user, their role and its scopes.
get.description: Allowed while a password change is pending, so the dashboard can tell the user to change it.

post.summary: Change the caller's password.
post.description: Needs the current password. The new one needs `Auth:Password:MinLength` characters (12) and nothing else (`400 invalid-password`). A wrong current password answers `400 current-password-incorrect` and counts toward lockout. On success the security stamp rotates (older access tokens stop working), `mustChangePassword` is cleared, every other refresh token of the user is revoked, and a new access token is returned; the current refresh cookie stays valid.

200.description: Changed. Use the access token in this answer from now on.

423.description: `locked-out`: too many wrong passwords; `Retry-After` says for how long.

get.summary: List users.
get.description: Ordered by email. A bad `role`, `disabled`, `page` or `pageSize` answers `400`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text found in the email or the display name. `%` and `_` are literal.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only users holding this role.

parameters.name: disabled
parameters.description: Only disabled (`true`) or only enabled (`false`) users.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1 or more. Default 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: 1 to `SavedRequests:MaxListPageSize`. Default 25.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Create a user with a one-time temporary password.
post.description: The answer is `201` with the user and `temporaryPassword` (16 characters, shown once, never stored in plain text, `Cache-Control: no-store`). The user has `mustChangePassword: true` and exactly the role given. Email is case-insensitive and unique (`409 email-exists`). Recorded in `user_audit` as `created`.

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`: the body holds a temporary password.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: One user.
get.description: Includes `lastLoginUtc` and `lockedOutUntilUtc`. Never a password or a hash. The `ETag` is the value to send as `If-Match` on a patch.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

patch.summary: Change a user's display name, role or disabled flag.
patch.description: Needs `If-Match`. A role change replaces the old role in one save, so the user never holds zero or two roles. Changing the role or disabling the user rotates their security stamp (so their access tokens stop at once, not after the 30 s gate cache) and revokes all their refresh tokens; both are recorded in `user_audit` (`role-changed`, `disabled`, `enabled`). Demoting or disabling the only enabled admin answers `409 last-admin`, also when two admins do it to each other at the same moment (the admins are row-locked in one transaction). An admin cannot disable themselves (`409 cannot-disable-self`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The user's ETag from `GET /users/{id}` (Identity's concurrency stamp, in quotes). Missing answers `428 precondition-required`, a stale one `412 edited-by-someone-else`. Any failed sign-in of that user also changes it, so a `412` may only mean "reload".

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Issue a new one-time temporary password.
post.description: Sets `mustChangePassword`, rotates the security stamp and revokes all the user's refresh tokens, so their sessions end at once. The new password is in the answer once (`Cache-Control: no-store`). Recorded as `password-reset`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`: the body holds a temporary password.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Clear a lockout.
post.description: Clears the lockout and the failed-password count. Recorded as `unlocked` (SPEC-GAP T-1011, Q-89: the spec lists no kind for it).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: The `user_audit` rows about one user.
get.description: Newest first. `actor` is a user id (with `actorName`), `anonymous` for a failed sign-in, `bootstrap`, or `api-client:<id>`. `detail` holds addresses and reasons, never a password or a token.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1 or more. Default 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: 1 to `SavedRequests:MaxListPageSize`. Default 25.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Save a validate-and-post body for a person to review and post.
post.description: Saved-requests §6.1. The body is exactly the validate-and-post body; nothing is posted. Over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes` answers `413` and anything that is not one JSON object `400 not-a-json-object`; neither is stored. Every JSON object is stored as version 1, byte for byte, even when it cannot be read (`needsAttention: true`, the JSON path in `validation.errors`) or when validation refuses it (`dryRun`, `allowModelAccounts`, control-total mismatch, too many rows) or holds rows. When validation cannot run (rules file missing, lists unreadable) the snapshot is `unavailable` and the save still succeeds. A request that looks like another one is flagged (`duplicate`), never refused. `createdBy` and `updatedBy` come from the caller, never the body. Treat any `201` as success.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Honoured per source (§10.1), by the store rather than the replay file: the same key and body answer `200` with the existing record and save nothing; the same key with a different body answers `409 idempotency-key-reused`. At most 128 characters.

200.description: The same `Idempotency-Key` and body were saved before: the existing record (`Idempotency-Replayed: true`).

400.description: `not-a-json-object`: the body is not one JSON object (or not UTF-8); nothing was saved. `invalid-request`: the `Idempotency-Key` is too long.

409.description: `idempotency-key-reused`: this source used the key for a different body; nothing was saved.

413.description: The body is over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes`; nothing was saved.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: List saved requests, filtered and paged.
get.description: Saved-requests §6.5. Every value is checked: an unknown `status` or `sort`, a flag that is not `true`/`false`, a date that is not `yyyy-MM-dd`, or a page outside its range answers `400`. Rows hold everything in the detail except the payload, the validation findings and the read errors.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Repeatable. Only these statuses.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only requests that do (`true`) or do not (`false`) need attention.

parameters.name: duplicate
parameters.description: Only flagged (`true`) or unflagged (`false`) requests.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text in the reference, the public reference, or a payee or memo inside the payload.

parameters.name: createdFrom
parameters.description: Created on or after this date (UTC).

parameters.name: createdTo
parameters.description: Created on or before this date (UTC).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `api-client:<clientId>` or `user:<userId>`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Default `-created`; a leading `-` is descending.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1 or more. Default 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: 1 to `SavedRequests:MaxListPageSize` (100). Default 25.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: Counts for the dashboard header.
get.description: Every status appears in `byStatus`, zero included.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: One saved request: latest payload, flags, validation snapshot and last attempt.
get.description: Saved-requests §6.2. The `ETag` is the row version, to send as `If-Match` on an edit or a post. `allowedActions` follows the status and the caller's scopes; an API key never gets an action. Actors are `{ id, name, email }` for a user and `{ id, name }` for an API client (`api-client:<id>`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

put.summary: Replace the payload of a pending saved request; the old payload stays as an earlier version.
put.description: Saved-requests §6.3, §8. The body is `{ "payload": { ...the full validate-and-post body... }, "note": "..." }`: a full payload, not a patch. `If-Match` is required. A payload that differs from the current one becomes version n+1 with its change list (numbers are compared as decimals, so `184.3` and `184.30` are equal), validation and the duplicate rules run again, and an `edited` event is written. An identical payload answers `200` and writes nothing. An unreadable payload is stored and flagged like a save. The API never recalculates `controlTotal`: change it together with an amount, or validation reports the mismatch. Only a `pending` request can be edited.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The row version from the last `GET` (its `ETag`), in quotes.

note.description: Why it was changed; kept with the version.

200.description: The saved request after the edit (or unchanged, when the payload was identical).

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

400.description: `not-a-json-object`: the body is not an object with a `payload` object (or not UTF-8); nothing was stored. `invalid-request`: `note` is not text.

409.description: `not-editable`: the request is not `pending`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the `If-Match` row version is not the current one. The body carries the current `rowVersion` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it. Nothing was changed.

413.description: The body is over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes`; nothing was stored.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Re-run validation and the duplicate rules for the current version and store the new snapshot.
post.description: Saved-requests §6.4. Takes no body. Rules, lists and the ledger change after a snapshot was taken, so this refreshes it (`validation.validatedUtc` moves) and writes a `validated` event. It bumps the row version, so an `ETag` held before goes stale. The snapshot is advisory: Post always validates again. Only a `pending` request can be validated.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

200.description: The saved request with its refreshed snapshot.

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

409.description: `not-editable`: the request is not `pending`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Discard a pending saved request, with a reason; an admin can restore it.
post.description: Saved-requests §7.1. The body is `{ "reason": "..." }`, 1 to 500 characters after trimming. The reason is kept as `discardReason` and in a `discarded` event. A discarded request is never posted and is not compared for duplicates. `If-Match` is optional here; when sent, it must be the current row version.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The row version from the last `GET`, in quotes. Optional.

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

400.description: `invalid-request`: the reason is missing, blank or over 500 characters; nothing was changed.

409.description: `not-discardable`: the request is not `pending`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the `If-Match` row version is not the current one. The body carries the current `rowVersion` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it. Nothing was changed.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

post.summary: Return a discarded saved request to pending (admin only).
post.description: Saved-requests §7.1. Takes no body. Clears `discardReason` and writes a `restored` event. `If-Match` is optional; when sent, it must be the current row version.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The row version from the last `GET`, in quotes. Optional.

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

409.description: `not-restorable`: the request is not `discarded`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the `If-Match` row version is not the current one. The body carries the current `rowVersion` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it. Nothing was changed.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.description: Byte for byte, as UTF-8: key order, whitespace, escapes and duplicate keys are kept. Never re-serialised.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

get.description: Number, who, when, note and change count. Version 1 is the original.

get.description: A version that does not exist answers `404`.

get.description: Without the stored result; `GET .../attempts/{attemptId}` has it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

get.summary: One attempt with the full stored result.
get.description: `result` is the validate-and-post answer (200) or its problem body, stored as returned.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

parameters.name: attemptId
parameters.description: The attempt id.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: The timeline, newest first.
get.description: `created`, `flagged-duplicate`, `edited`, `validated`, `post-started`, `post-finished`, `discarded`, `restored`, `resolved`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: `X-Api-Key: <key>` — the header this build reads, and the one every operation is secured with here. Each key belongs to one caller in `clients.json` and carries only the scopes that caller was given; `x-required-scope` on every operation names the one it needs.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`: a dashboard user's JWT (saved-requests §11.3), not an API key. An API key still travels only in `X-Api-Key` (Q-67); sending both headers answers `400 ambiguous-credentials`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Replaying a request under the same key returns the stored answer and sends nothing to QuickBooks a second time; the same key with a different body is a 409.

BatchId.name: id
BatchId.description: Batch id. It contains `#`, which must be sent percent-encoded as `%23`.

JobId.name: id
JobId.description: Job id, derived from the job folder's name.

BadRequest.description: Malformed or self-inconsistent request. Nothing was posted.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or a key no caller holds.

Forbidden.description: The key is known but lacks the scope this operation needs.

Conflict.description: A state conflict, or an `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited; `Retry-After` says for how long.

Unavailable.description: QuickBooks or Hermes is unreachable or busy, or the app is not ready.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87).

lockedOutUntilUtc.description: Set only while a lockout is still running.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87).

lockedOutUntilUtc.description: Set only while a lockout is still running.

temporaryPassword.description: 16 characters from an unambiguous alphabet. Shown once; hand it over and it is gone.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87), and it then has no scopes.

mustChangePassword.description: While true every route except `me`, `change-password` and `logout` answers `403 password-change-required`.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem details. `requestId` is the same id as the `X-Request-Id` header and every log line of that request.

errors.description: Present when the failure is per item.

companyFile.description: Refused unless `QuickBooks:AllowCompanyFileOverride` is on and the path is inside `QuickBooks:AllowedCompanyFolders`.

requireBackup.description: Ask for a guarantee rather than a warning (T-917). `true` raises the `backupFreshness` check from warning to error, so a stale backup — or a server with no `QuickBooks:BackupFolder` configured, which cannot confirm one — makes `ok` false and the response 422. What the flag should mean was never specified; see Q-72.

reference.description: The caller's own name for this batch.

controlTotal.description: The caller's own sum over every submitted row. It is checked, never corrected: a mismatch refuses the whole batch and no amount is adjusted to make it agree.

allowModelAccounts.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED (T-915). Sending `true` is refused with 400: tiers 3-4 never run on the direct path, so the flag would silently do nothing. Give each row a `lineAccount`, or add a rule for its last four. Whether this is ever implemented is open question Q-51; the `qb:post:ai` scope is reserved for it and is checked nowhere today.

SyncPostRequest.description: `DirectRequest` minus `dryRun` (validate-and-post §4). The rows are identical, so a caller can move between the two posting routes without rewriting one.

reference.description: The caller's own name for this post; it names the ledger row `api-<reference>`.

controlTotal.description: Required here. The caller's own sum over every submitted row: checked to the cent, never corrected. A mismatch refuses the whole request and no amount is adjusted to make it agree.

dryRun.description: NOT A FIELD OF THIS ROUTE. Sending any value, `false` included, is refused with 400 `dry-run-not-supported` — a caller who asks for a dry run and is answered `posted` would have moved money they believed they were only checking. Use `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/transactions/validate` to check a batch without sending it.

allowModelAccounts.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED, as on the direct path (T-915): tiers 3-4 never run here, so the flag would silently do nothing. Sending it is refused with 400. Give each row a `lineAccount`, or add a rule for its last four (Q-51).

SyncPostResult.description: What landed in QuickBooks (validate-and-post §6.1). There is no `batchId`, `dryRun` or `isRunning`: this route has no batch to poll and no mode to choose.

postId.description: Names the ledger row, for `POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/undo`. It is NOT a polling resource — no `GET` accepts it. It contains `#`, which must be sent percent-encoded as `%23`.

status.description: `posted` on the ordinary path: a held row is a 422 before anything is sent. It can still read `partial` or `failed` if a gate that runs after the SDK was touched (G4's live half, G5) refused a row — a caller whose money half-moved is told, not reassured.

skipped.description: Rows a skip rule or G4 excluded; why `posted` can be below `submitted` on a clean post.

externalId.description: The caller's own key, echoed so a batch can be reconciled against their records.

txnId.description: QuickBooks' own id for the transaction.

held.description: Empty on the ordinary path; a held row is a 422 before anything is sent.

SyncPostProblem.description: The 422 of validate-and-post §6.2: RFC 7807, with every finding in `validation` — not the first, because one held row refuses the whole request and a caller must be able to fix them all in one pass.

detail.description: e.g. `3 of 134 row(s) would be held; nothing was sent to QuickBooks.`

postable.description: Rows that would have posted — and did not, because of the ones below.

postedIn.description: For `already-posted`: the earlier batch that posted this row.

unknownNames.description: Names this request would send that `qb-lists.json` does not have.

externalId.description: The caller's key. Echoed and stored; never used to decide identity.

amount.description: Positive, at most two decimals. The direction comes from `kind`.

account.description: The bank or credit-card account the money moves on.

lineAccount.description: The expense or income account; rules resolve it when it is left out.

last4.description: Last four digits of the account; part of the fingerprint.

TxnKind.description: `check` and `deposit` move money on a bank account; `ccCharge` and `ccCredit` on a credit card; `skip` leaves the row alone. Read case-insensitively.

counts.description: `wouldPost + held + skipped` is `submitted`, so the arithmetic of the answer can be checked too. `duplicates` is part of `skipped`.

unknownNames.description: Names in the batch that `qb-lists.json` does not have.

PlanRow.description: One submitted row and what would become of it.

requestId.description: First 16 characters of the row's fingerprint.

reason.description: The hold or skip code, e.g. `no-account-rule`, `already-in-quickbooks`.

batchId.description: The earlier batch this row already posted in.

posted.description: The money that actually moved; zero for a dry run.

unavailable.description: Nothing was sent: QuickBooks could not be reached, or the backup guard refused. Safe to retry.

location.description: Poll this for the finished batch.

missingInRules.description: Names QuickBooks has that `rules.json` says nothing about.

QbLists.description: The cached QuickBooks names (`qb-lists.json`). Empty lists with a null `syncedUtc` mean the sync has not run.

ok.description: The folder would become a job and no statement was held.

errors.description: Why the folder cannot become a job (F1). Empty when it can.

unreadable.description: Files that will not be read, and why (F4).

layout.description: The `CsvLayouts` name, or `hermes-t2` for a PDF.

reconcile.description: The G1 verdict: `{ ok, verified, message }`.

totals.description: The statement's own printed figures (PDF only).

force.description: Re-run a folder that already finished.

fragment.description: A fragment of the statement description, matched case-insensitively.

name.description: The QuickBooks vendor or customer name.

account.description: A QuickBooks account name; checked against `qb-lists.json` when it exists.

previous.description: What the rule said before; null when it is new.

SavedRequestActor.description: Who did it (§5.3). Users are disabled, never deleted, so an id always has a name.

SavedRequestValidation.description: §6.4. Advisory: Post always validates again. `needsAttention` is set by `unreadable`, `held` and `refused`, not by `unavailable`.

errors.description: Request-level refusals, or the read errors (`$.path: message`).

reason.description: Only when `unavailable`: why validation could not run.

SavedRequestSummary.description: §6.5: the detail without the payload, the findings and the read errors.
